title: Newton’s Method
lead: Most equations f(x) = 0 have no formula for their solutions. This section approximates a root by following tangent lines down to the x-axis, one after another, shows how that process can fail, and looks at other processes that repeat one function to generate a list of numbers.
objectives: Describe the steps of Newton’s method.
Explain what an iterative process means.
Recognize when Newton’s method does not work.
Apply iterative processes to various situations.
summary_html:
• Newton’s method approximates roots of $\kf(x)=0$ by starting with an initial approximation ${x}_{0},$ then uses tangent lines to the graph of $\kf$ to create a sequence of approximations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\text{,\ldots}.$
  • Typically, Newton’s method is an efficient method for finding a particular root. In certain cases, Newton’s method fails to work because the list of numbers ${x}_{0},{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\text{,\ldots}$ does not approach a finite value or it approaches a value other than the root sought.
  • Any process in which a list of numbers ${x}_{0},{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\text{,\ldots}$ is generated by defining an initial number ${x}_{0}$ and defining the subsequent numbers by the equation ${x}_{n}=\kF({x}_{n-1})$ for some function $\kF$ is an iterative process. Newton’s method is an example of an iterative process, where the function $\kF(x)=x-[\frac{f(x)}{\kfprime(x)}]$ for a given function $\kf.$

Newton’s method can be used to find maxima and minima of functions in addition to the roots. In this case apply Newton’s method to the derivative function ${f}^{'}(x)$ to find its roots, instead of the original function. For the following exercises, consider the formulation of the method.

To find candidates for maxima and minima, we need to find the critical points ${f}^{'}(x)=0.$ Show that to solve for the critical points of a function $f(x),$ Newton’s method is given by ${x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{'}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{''}({x}_{n})}.$

answer.solution: The critical points are the solutions of $f'(x)=0,$ so apply Newton’s method to the function $g(x)=f'(x).$ Its derivative is $g'(x)=f''(x),$ so Newton’s formula $x_{n+1}=x_{n}-\frac{g(x_{n})}{g'(x_{n})}$ becomes $x_{n+1}=x_{n}-\frac{f'(x_{n})}{f''(x_{n})}.$

For the following exercises, use the specified method to solve the equation. If it does not work, explain why it does not work.

Newton’s method, ${x}^{2}+2=0$

answer.solution: It does not work: $x^{2}+2\ge 2$ for every real $x,$ so the equation has no real solution and there is no root for the approximations to approach. Newton’s formula $x_{n+1}=x_{n}-\frac{x_{n}^{2}+2}{2x_{n}}=\frac{x_{n}}{2}-\frac{1}{x_{n}}$ produces numbers that keep jumping about without settling, and the step is undefined whenever some $x_{n}=0,$ where the tangent line is horizontal.

exercises.prompt:
For the following exercises, use the specified method to solve the equation. If it does not work, explain why it does not work.

Newton’s method, $0=1+{x}^{2}$ starting at ${x}_{0}=0$

answer.solution: It does not work. With $f(x)=1+x^{2},$ $f'(x)=2x,$ so $f'(0)=0:$ the tangent line at $x_{0}=0$ is horizontal and never meets the $x$-axis, and $x_{1}=x_{0}-\frac{f(x_{0})}{f'(x_{0})}$ is undefined. Besides, $1+x^{2}\ge 1,$ so the equation has no real solution at all.

For the following exercises, use the secant method, an alternative iterative method to Newton’s method. The formula is given by

${x}_{n}={x}_{n-1}-f({x}_{n-1})\frac{{x}_{n-1}-{x}_{n-2}}{f({x}_{n-1})-f({x}_{n-2})}.$

Why would you use the secant method over Newton’s method? What are the necessary restrictions on $f?$

answer.solution: The secant method needs only values of $f,$ not its derivative, so it is useful when $f'$ is hard or costly to compute; it pays for that by needing two starting values and usually more iterations. It requires $f$ to be continuous near the root and $f(x_{n-1})\ne f(x_{n-2})$ at every step, so that the formula never divides by zero.

assumes.text: $({x}_{1},0)$ is the $x$-intercept of the tangent line to $\kf$ at ${x}_{0}.$
Each ${x}_{n}$ is the $x$-intercept of the tangent line to $\kf$ at ${x}_{n-1},$ where $\kfprime({x}_{n-1})\ne 0.$

steps.cap: Each step repeats the first, from ${x}_{n-1}$ in place of ${x}_{0}.$
